ideas.evidence: live.py:1476 (_render: headerless passes are never combined with the store); associate.py:331-352 (rules 2 and 3 take any z/w); a rule-3 test against 30 accumulators takes 0.45 s (opt/live-ops/m3_store_scale.py). e2e-results.md: 8 passes at -20 dB combine to +5.6 dB, so a pass that shows nothing alone becomes visible combined.
ideas.expected_gain: Inferred: on a repeat pass, the operator sees the combined picture and the callsign 15-25 minutes earlier. Stored results are unchanged.
ideas.cost: Small to moderate.
ideas.risk: A wrong early match would show the wrong picture, hence 'tentative'. corr_accept's expected_t scales with the evidence, so a partial pass gives a weaker test, not a looser one.

ideas.title: Warn when an own send would blank a due segment of a picture being received

The listener could mark those slots 'own send' instead of 'lost'.

Per ui-handoff.md, whether the QRSS window should keep listening during an own pass is still open with Jeff.

ideas.cost: Small: due slots in state.json plus a warning in the schedule dialog.
ideas.risk: None to decoding; UI only.

ideas.title: Measure L's header thresholds: block only, spread copy only, and both
ideas.what: Spec 5 still gives L's header as an estimate of about -27 dB and says 'neither is measured yet'. Measure as was done for CE, on L_MEDIUM or L_FULL (l-short has too few data symbols): steady, then quiet and moderate, from the stored diagnostic llr_block / llr_spread. Put the numbers in the spec. Add one slow-tier test of block-only, spread-only and both decodes; it also gives the fallback rescue rate nobody has measured. This decides F3 (rho), whether L1/F1's deeper acquisition is matched by header depth, and how far the estimate is off.

ideas.risk: None.
ideas.onair_compat: n/a (the spec owner edits the spec text)

ideas.title: Measure gate V's noise tail at Z_ACCEPT for each waveform, blind and timed, offline
ideas.what: Gate V's false-accept rate is asserted from Z_ref being N(0,1) on noise (about 1e-9 to 1e-8 per candidate), but the recorded distributions disagree in both directions. Run offline H0 campaigns per waveform with fit=True and fit=False, including the real false population: mis-timed real signals, CE sideband ghosts, the L -1/T_L alias and other stations. Start with TINY frames and confirm on a smaller FULL sample. Then either keep Z_ACCEPT = 6, raise it for blind L, or lower it for CE (flag or Jeff's OK).
ideas.evidence: constants.py:64 (Z_ACCEPT 6.0); track.py:1386-1392 (the V_TIMING_TRIES comment's 1e-9 to 1e-8). wfB_parts.txt:109, 159 and 178: blind L gate V on noise has mean 0.52, sd 1.16, max 3.17 over 20 seeds, 'the false-accept rate per blind candidate is unknown'; blind CE mean 0.19; timed Z_ref sd 0.62 (L) and 0.50 (CE). A Gaussian with the blind-L moments puts 6 at 4.7 sigma, about 1e-6 per candidate (inferred), a thousand times the design figure. README known limitations: CE blind at quiet -34 dB finds 0/10, with Z_ref about 4 even at the true timing.
ideas.expected_gain: Either a measured false-accept rate for blind L (it may need a higher threshold), or, if CE's tail allows, 20log10(6/T) dB of blind depth: 1.6 dB at T = 5 and 2.5 dB at T = 4.5 (inferred).
ideas.cost: TINY first: blind fit_timing_l takes 0.06 s, so about 5000 channels is 10-15 minutes, in 3-4 runs of under 5 minutes. FULL: 60-80 s per gate, so 1000 gates is about 20 CPU-hours. Offline only, never CI.
ideas.risk: None for the code. A white-noise-only calibration would be optimistic, which is why the real false population must be included.
ideas.changes_ce_results: n/a (measurement); any threshold change needs a flag or Jeff's OK

ideas.title: Measure the L ghost rule, and reconcile GHOST_HZ (20) with L's 22.07 Hz band

ideas.title: Spec: state that the signal is USB (audio = RF minus dial)
ideas.what: Spec rev 13 never says which sideband to use; README.md:273 and 60m.md:15 assume USB. A listener on LSB, such as a WebSDR or KiwiSDR that defaults to LSB below 10 MHz, hears a mirror image. For L the data then sits above the pilot and A2-L never matches. For CE the linear phase term flips sign while the carrier does not, so references read negative and gate V refuses the pass. Add one sentence to the spec. Optionally, behind a flag, let the receiver retry a failed candidate on the conjugate of the front-end signal.
ideas.evidence: grep finds no sideband statement in qrsstvae-options.md; docs/qrss/README.md:273 ('the RF frequency for USB'); demod.py:83 (y = Im(m conj(u))/(K|u|^2), which a mirrored CE pass negates). The mirroring analysis is inferred, not run.
ideas.expected_gain: Inferred: turns a total loss into a normal reception for a listener on the wrong sideband.
ideas.cost: One sentence for the spec owner. A conjugate retry doubles A2/A3 work for failed candidates only.
ideas.risk: A conjugate retry doubles the false-candidate chances, hence the flag.
ideas.onair_compat: The spec sentence changes nothing on the air; fielded listeners and the C beacon are unaffected.

insights: L's weak pilot is the common root of most L receiver weaknesses, while gate V is where L is strong. The pilot carries 13.8% of the power, and 10.5% in the preamble, where the clipper squeezes it to gain 0.656 against 0.708 in the data. CE's carrier carries about 51-53%. That one fact explains the A1 limit (about -26 dB live, while A2-L passes 8/8 at -31) and the 1.2-1.8 dB round-A loss on moderate fading, which is pilot-track noise: using the true pilot gain as the data gain costs only 0.05-0.10 dB (design.md:935, 945). It also explains the per-pass gain-scale spread (k 0.83-1.49 at -24..-28 dB, against CE's 0.92-1.04, opt/buildrec/m_rounds.py), A3's roughly 6 dB gap, and refine_path_l switching off by -16 dB. Meanwhile L's Z_ref at equal average power is about 1.5x CE's (95 against 62 at -12 dB). So for L the binding stage has moved from gate V to A1 and A3.

For L, finding passes, not combining or demodulating them, is the limit. Combining works: 8 passes at -20 dB combine to the ideal 9 dB (e2e-results.md), and two header copies go 2.4 dB deeper against an ideal 3. L's 16-pass good picture needs each pass found at about -29.6 dB. A3 found L_FULL at -28 and -30 dB but not at -34, and hinted A2-L gets 8/8 at -31 and 2/8 at -34. CE's 16-pass point is -26.4 dB, and blind detection found every CE pass tried at -32 dB (spec 5.1, rev 12). That is roughly 6 dB of detection margin for CE against 0-4 dB for L. L's realised multi-pass gain therefore depends on hints finding nearly every repeat, and on the L template search, which does not exist yet.

The lead-in is L's cheapest acquisition lever, and it is already in the format. Ten seconds of pilot at full average power carries about 6 dB more pilot energy than the whole preamble's 10.5% share. Two independent measurements (l-short with 8 seeds, l-tiny with 12) put A1 about 5 dB deeper once the A1 window reaches back over the lead-in. By contrast, more A1 lines are not the cure that lesson 2 suggested. Going from 16 to 64 lines adds 0-3 of 20 detections between -24 and -29 dB, and at -29 dB it is the 1e-4 threshold, not the line count, that loses the pilot (opt/docs-spec/a1_rank2.py).

L buys bandwidth, not dB, at a fixed peak. Its one-pass good picture is -14.0 dB against CE's -10.9 at equal average power, but -10.8 against -10.9 at equal peak. The app uses one peak-scaled transmit level for everything (tx_panel.cpp:1583), so L always runs at CE's PEP and its 3.2-3.4 dB average-power edge cannot be used today. At -10 dB on SHORT, L's mean W was +7.75 dB against CE's +5.94: +1.8 dB, already capped by its 12.2 dB clipper SINR and the pre-header spread copy.

Clipper self-noise matters only where L is not meant to operate. With the scrambler and precoder it averages down across passes like channel noise. L's 12.2 dB clipper SINR therefore costs about 0.75 dB at one pass (W about +5 dB) and under 0.05 dB at 16 passes near -29.6 dB (computed). The spec's 0 dB threshold is tuned for single strong passes. The clipper is close to a hard limit even at 8 kHz: the maximum is 3.20-3.24 dB against 3.15 dB at the 99.99% point, and nothing exceeds 3.5 dB in 13M samples. So a plain peak scale costs only about 0.07 dB.

The clipper treats sections unequally. Constant-amplitude preamble and header QPSK keep gain 1.006 and 16.9 dB SINR, while Gaussian data drops to gain 0.889 and 12.2 dB (opt/transmit/m2_peaks.py). L's header is therefore probably deeper than its data-like -27 dB estimate; CE's equivalent estimate was 5 dB pessimistic. And preamble-time A1 is 0.66 dB worse off than a uniform pilot would be. The spread copy is the most expensive constant L inherited: free for CE once the header is known, it costs every L latent 0.23 dB permanently, and its gain on L has not been measured.

The receiver's spacing constants were sized for 50 Hz CE and do not scale to L's packing. They include the 45 Hz neighbour guard, the 85-120 Hz noise windows, 16 A1 lines at 10 Hz, GHOST_HZ = 20 (L's band reaches 22.07 Hz below its pilot) and MERGE_HZ = 5. At the spec's 30 Hz L spacing, one neighbour 90 Hz away already covers a whole noise window. That is the KC2G failure (Z_ref about 1, against 8-11 with the neighbour excluded) waiting to recur. The receiver, not the waveform, limits how densely L can pack.

The band-edge 'SNR reads too high' problem is purely a noise-estimate problem. The front end is flat to within 0.01 dB at 326 Hz and 0.29 dB at 300 Hz, so the signal is intact. But the noise bins 85-120 Hz away sit 12-30 dB down in the filter's skirt, so SNR reads 6.9 dB high at 326 Hz and 8.4 dB high at 305 (opt/rxcode/m3_edge_cpu.py). The front end's flat region is about 310-2690 Hz, not the 250-2750 Hz the build notes assumed; it is already -6 dB at 250 and 2750 Hz.

A pass's frequency at t0, the spline's end value, is a poor report on both waveforms. On moderate fading with zero-mean Doppler it read +0.40/+0.66/-0.23 Hz off (L) and +0.41/+0.56 Hz off (CE), and +1.09 Hz on a weak steady L pass, while the frame median stayed within 0.031 Hz in all 13 cases. KC2G's real carrier is not a line either: 1205.40 Hz at 17 s and 1206.0-1206.65 Hz in the last 10 min, +0.030 Hz/min with 0.22 Hz rms. Yet two passes 30 min apart have the same t0 intercept, 1205.459 Hz, which looks like a warm-up chirp restarting at each key-up (n=2, tentative). The stored 1206.082 Hz was 0.62 Hz off, so the 0.5 Hz error on Andrew's reception is most likely this end-value artifact, not ionospheric Doppler. Timing moves between passes (0.72 s, then 0.82-0.90 s), so any cross-pass prior can only use frequency.

EM and data-aided re-tracking measure small on both waveforms, unlike the models of them. CE: '--em 1' left W at +5.64 dB and cost 229 s (e2e-results.md); the README gives +0.0 to +0.15 dB against the spec's +0.5. L (opt/live-ops/m2_l_em.py): at most +0.38 dB accumulated at -12 dB, and about +-0.2 dB at -20 dB. Without a block split the pass's own SNR rises 1-2 dB, almost all of it the prior confirming itself; with the split the honest gain is +0.05 to +0.19 dB. The spec model (+5.2 dB for L) and the transmit lens's model (0.7-1.9 dB at 16-64 passes) are not borne out where measured; -28 dB has not been tested. What does pay is knowing the header (round B): +1.0 dB at -12 dB and +1.8 at -6 for L, +0.8 at -12 for CE, and +0.1-0.5 dB slope-corrected at -24/-28 dB.

Latent SNR measured by mean squared error rewards a z that has been shrunk. In the chain runs, round A seemed to beat the header-known genie at -24..-28 dB (-6.37 against -7.57 dB at -28, scratch_chain/extra.txt). But z was 17% low there (k = 0.826); slope-corrected it is -7.99 dB, worse than round B's -7.50. In the joint estimator z is unbiased given a correct u_hat (demod.py:208-219), so any slope k other than 1 is the tracker's gain scale, which is a useful way to split the error. Quote slope-corrected or honest-weighted figures. Mean W reading above the latent SNR (+3.94 against +1.81 dB) is arithmetic against harmonic averaging, not miscalibration (mean(w·e^2) is 0.97-1.07). Single-seed W-honesty figures are noise (1.075 against 0.962 for two seeds), so use 3-5 seeds per cell.

Estimators inherited from CE turned out biased in proportion to how much L's references feed its gain track. CE's kappa form read 0.2-0.7 on L where the honest value was 0.9-1.2, overstating W by up to 1.7 dB on moderately fading L (D34). Regression dilution makes |delta| read about 9% high at -27 dB. The textbook errors-in-variables correction overshot on fading (0.81 at -20 dB moderate), so TRK left the biased estimator in place; a known-symbol scale fit is the safer fix.

Live CPU does not follow progress. A refresh at 5% heard costs as much as one at 95% (29.8 against 30.0 CPU s for one CE FULL signal at -12 dB), because the tracker and gate run over the whole frame with the unheard future filled with noise and erased afterwards. CPU is also set by different stages in the two waveforms. In CE the scalar Python Kalman forward pass is 28-30% of receive time. In L it is 10%, since T_L = 2T gives half the positions, and the data-band matched-filter gather leads instead. L's tracker is still not cheaper than CE's (round A on FULL 7.25 s against 6.33; gate V 10.9 s against 13.3). The +64% cost of listening for both waveforms lies in acquisition and refused gates, mostly on CE sidebands. Profiling pairs must be warmed or interleaved: running CE-only first made it look 45% more expensive than the joint run.

Every CE signal at -15 dB or stronger appears in A3 as three lines: its carrier and sidebands about ±12 Hz away. The +12 Hz sideband has an unmistakable L shape (z1 +112 to +593), and the CE carrier can be gated a second time as an 'L copy', because only candidates within MERGE_HZ (5 Hz) are skipped. On SHORT, the refused sideband gates cost 4-7x the real gate. Spectral shape otherwise separates the waveforms cheaply. L's z1 is +155/+50/+16 at -15/-20/-25 dB, against |z1| at most 2.3 for CE and a standard deviation of 1.025 on noise. L's band energy is still visible at -34 dB on L_FULL (z1 5.0), where A3's pilot-only emission no longer finds it, so the A3 gap is in the emission model, not the signal.

The D3 residual ratio is a near-perfect waveform discriminator. CE's own tracks give R 0.55-2.16, fading included; an L signal under CE's gate gives 3.6-15.4; CE's sideband ghosts give 5.2-6.2. Because L's values overlap the ghost band, the rule needs both R > 2 and Z/sqrt(R) <= 6, and dropping P from the residual model would wrongly reject real fading CE passes (R 2.43 and 3.22). So fielded CE-only listeners will not fail on L, they will misreport it: junk tiles at z 7.2-7.3 with latents near -8 dB, each also becoming a junk provisional cluster in that station's store.

Aliases differ per waveform. CE's symbol-rate aliases sit at ±33 Hz, while L's -1/T_L alias lies 16.49 Hz below its pilot, inside its own data band, and it passed A2-L 12/12 at -6 dB. CE's alias handling therefore cannot simply be reused for L, and L's ghost rule is still unmeasured.

Building L exposed pre-existing CE bugs. associate._soft_header decoded an empty LLR sum on headerless frames, so --just-ce failed to store its second TINY pass. CE's refine_timing carries a sum|m|^2 noise term in its likelihood and gives up on an indefinite Hessian; both flaws showed up only under L's weaker references. The joint end-to-end run was a stronger test of the shared code than either waveform's own suite.

Multi-pass association grows quadratically and runs under the listener lock: 14.16 s for one header-decoded pass at 30 accumulators x 59 provisional clusters, about 8 ms per pair (opt/live-ops/m3_store_scale.py). CE and L passes of one picture already combine with no extra work. picture_id hashes the codec, mode and latents with no waveform in it (picture.py:113-120), the soft header uses the same 2,474 coded bits for both, and store.twin compares band centres across waveforms. Two gaps remain. store.due predicts later passes only 'for the same waveform at the same frequency'. And CE's header LLRs read about 0.85 of honest scale, against L's own-class scaling, so mixed-waveform soft-header sums under-weight CE.

Erasure costs far more than weakness for this decoder: 'half a pass at +3 dB is worth a whole pass at -3.6 dB' (decoder-measurements.md). That argues for sending the 2,200 never-sent latents (+0.3 dB at the good level) and for weakening marginal data rather than gating it. Identification by matching beats identification by reading: at -20 dB the Morse callsign was read in 2 of 17 passes, but the match statistic against a known callsign agreed in 17 of 17.

On fading paths CE's header is limited by tracking, not by code strength. With both copies it decodes at -30.3 dB steady, -29.0 dB quiet and -26.9 dB moderate, and gate V fails to fit the timing at -28 dB moderate. Coding changes such as a larger list size therefore help most on steady paths.

Several transmit parameters were checked and are not worth changing. CE's beta of 0.8: 1.0 rad would gain 0.2 dB at 16 passes but drop the carrier from 53% to 37% of power and widen the 99% band from 51.5 to 60 Hz. Si5351 synthesis error sits 43 dB below the latents. RRC roll-off sets no SNR. The preamble is 1.1% of the frame, with only about 7 s of slack before the next pass's full lead-in. Dropping from four callsign windows to three would save only about 0.03 dB.

The build records' 'L preamble is 6 ms longer' is wrong. Both preambles last 20.00625 s (660 x 0.0303125 = 330 x 0.060625; constants.py:38 and 74), but only by construction. A change to either preamble must update acquire.live_end_s, or the live candidate cache (live.py:1185) freezes before the L preamble ends.

Half duplex keeps the QRSS listener process running through our own send but feeds it no audio (the ring is set to nullptr, qrss_window.cpp:676-683). Slots covered by our own send are lost from the ring and from the passband store alike.

The SNR2500 estimate reads 0.3-0.9 dB low in every simulated end-to-end case (e2e-results.md). That is a consistent reporting bias, not a decoding loss, so SNR figures quoted from the listener in the field are probably pessimistic by about that much (inferred).

Mutation testing is what made the build's tests trustworthy. The DEM builder's tests caught 13 of 22 injected changes; ACQ's first pass left 11 of 20 mutants alive; INT-RX left 6 of 77. Test time is under pressure: L added 33.5 s to the default QRSS tier before six tests moved to slow, and test_qrss_lacquire alone runs 7.4-13.5 s against a 5 s target.
